# Re-rank 14 proposal (D148)

## Before order

210, 211, 216, 220, 221, 222, 223, 224, 225, 213, 217, 218, 212, 215, 206, 207

## After order

228, 229, 210, 211, 216, 220, 221, 222, 223, 224, 225, 213, 217, 218, 212, 215, 206, 207

## Next card

228 — hidden, encoded and non-shell delete forms, plus the contents of files a seat writes, because the deletion-ban corrective remains open and the scan must cover the real forms that slipped past 227 before any other work outruns it.

## One-line rationale

The 227 corrective is not finished until the scan covers the real deletion forms and the seat-written script cases, and 229 is next because a working Copilot route prevents every decision seat from being wasted while quota is available.

## What changed against note 13

- Card 227 is closed and removed from the active queue.
- Card 228 is inserted at the front as the direct safety follow-up from the 227 deletion-ban failure, keeping the corrective in the same thread rather than splitting it again.
- Card 229 is inserted immediately behind it to unblock the Decider gate while Copilot is available; it is a process blocker, not a product card. 
- The rest of the order stays in note 13's sequence, with 210 before 211 because the record-checker conflict and the hash-looking Decider id are still active open defects in the checker path.

## Reversals I state

- I reverse the earlier idea that 210/211 must keep their note-13 order ahead of all new ready cards; 228 and 229 are the new front-rank corrective and gate-fix work.
- I do not split 228 into a scan card plus a push-detector card; the last re-rank already decided that one corrective card should cover both the deletion-ban failure and the scan follow-up.
- I do not leave 229 behind the older queue because the decision-seat gate is a hard blocker when Copilot is available; the queue should not waste every decision seat while that is open.
- If the checker hardening is shown to be materially worse than the prompt-truncation fix in the next audit, 210 may move ahead of 229; as of this rerank, 229's seat-preventing failure is the more immediate blocker.

## Where cards 228 and 229 go

- Card 228 goes first: it is the direct continuation of the 227 corrective and the specific scan blind-spot fix under the product owner's safety ruling.
- Card 229 goes second: it fixes the decision-seat gate itself, and with Copilot available every other decision seat is wasted until it lands.

## Follow-on note

This keeps the safety corrective first, then the gate fix, then the open-checker and template work. It preserves note 13's ordering for the rest of the backlog while moving the two newly-ready corrective cards to the front of the queue.

## Facilitator note (open FAILs and the corrective-card gate)
- Audit 106 (2026-11-01 00:33 UTC, .mob/audits/last.json, read only) lists open FAILs MD-003, MD-010, F-071, F-072 and F-074. Its summary also names a "collision bug, detect ruling, wiki override unrecorded". F-072 and F-074 and those three items never reached the facilitator; their ledger text is not in the repository. They are asked of the product owner now, and this note will be corrected when they arrive.
- The corrective-card gate starts only a card that names an open FAIL. Card 228 names F-071; card 210 names MD-003; card 211 names MD-010. Card 229 names none (it was filed as an MD-002 rotation corrective, and MD-002 is no longer open). If F-072 or F-074 turns out to be the Copilot no-vote, 229 names it and keeps its place; otherwise it waits behind 210 and 211 until the FAILs close.

## Adopted condition (round 1, D145; the architect, backend developer, independent reviewer (audit lens) and delivery lead, one condition in four wordings)
Card 229 moves behind 210 and 211, because it names no open FAIL and the corrective-card gate would not start it. It moves up again only if F-072 or F-074 is confirmed as the Copilot no-vote and the card names it. After order: 228, 210, 211, 229, 216, 220, 221, 222, 223, 224, 225, 213, 217, 218, 212, 215, 206, 207. Next card: 228. The delivery lead's further point (228 within D136) is the standing commit rule and needs no adoption. The re-poll may not add new demands.
